column1: # gates/gate-required-floor.tsv - THE MONOTONIC FLOOR UNDER THE GATE MANIFEST'S `required` COUNT, AND THE DIGEST
# OF THE REQUIRED SET. Seeded #549, 2026-11-06, for item (36):
# jobs/468-the-floor-and-the-digest-fix-are-built-and-controlled-and-held-on-the-detector-they-added-2026-10-03.
# Designed and controlled at #467 and #468 on branch claude/cool-noether-me7uq8 (c69a304), where this file was
# seeded at 49 and NEVER LANDED; the mechanism is rebuilt here by hand, onto a gatemanifest.sh that has since
# gained the committed-self anchor. The branch's seed row is NOT carried: it described a 49-gate tree.
# THE DEFECT IT CLOSES. The manifest's own `required` count is the suite's denominator and nothing bounded it from
# below: delete a gate, flip its row to `absent`, type any reason into field 7, and `gatemanifest.sh check`
# reported one fewer required gate and exited 0 (measured at #467 on 21-review-brilliant.js, the only cover for
# brilliancy explanations). The committed-self anchor (#540/#544) now catches that edit against origin/main - but
# only where git can answer, and only for a weakening that has not already landed. This register needs neither.
# THE MECHANISM. Append-only, like gates/build-numbers.tsv and gates/held-trees.tsv, with a CHAIN FIELD: every
# row carries the floor that stood BEFORE it (field 2), so row i's prev must equal row i-1's floor and an edited or
# deleted INTERIOR row is a hard failure with no git. Field 9 is a digest of the sorted REQUIRED gate names
# (sha256, first 12 hex), so a SWAP at constant count - promote a known-absent row, de-require a real gate - is
# visible although no count moves [#467, antagonist A's 5.1]. Field 9 is ALWAYS 12 hex: there is no `-` sentinel,
# because on the branch one `-` in it switched the set check off with no message [#468, antagonist B's F1].
# THE RULES `gatemanifest.sh check` ENFORCES: row 1 is kind `seed`; a `raise` increases the floor; a `lower`
# decreases it by EXACTLY ONE, carries a reason in field 7, and names in field 8 a gate whose manifest state is
# `retired` (one gate leaves per row, so one row cannot account for twenty removals - #467, B's F1 and F2); the
# tree's required count is >= the last floor and its required-set digest equals the last row's; and the rows
# committed at origin/main (or HEAD) are a PREFIX of the rows here.
# THE TWO RESIDUALS, NAMED. (1) That last rule is the only defence against a TRAILING TRUNCATION or a rewrite of
# ROW 1 - a chain cannot see either from inside the file - and it is only as good as git: where the anchor reads
# NOT CHECKED, deleting the last row lowers the floor silently. (2) `sync` records whatever set the tree has when
# the count RISES, so a de-require hidden behind two arrivals is recorded as a raise; the manifest anchor is what
# sees the de-required row in that case.
# WHO WRITES IT: `CT_BUILD=#NNN CT_RUNID=<runId> gates/gatemanifest.sh sync '<why>'` raises it;
# `... retire <gate.js> '<why>'` lowers it by one. Both REFUSE without CT_BUILD and CT_RUNID. `check` NEVER writes.
# A tree whose required set changed without either door (a hand-added row, a branch rebased under this file) is
# repaired by running sync: it raises the floor to the count that stands and records the set.
# floor  prev  kind   at          build  runId                   why                                   gate  reqset
